Metropolis-Hastings Traceplots and Burn-In

Before tackling multiple parameters in the Bayesian setting, we discussed trace plots and tracking convergence in the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm (also applicable to other MCMC algorithms).

The following code generated the plots that appear in the first half of Lecture 6. In it, we are attempting to acquire a sample from a standard normal N(0,1) using the MH algorithm.

mh_mcmc_norm <- function(n, theta=0.2, sd=0.2){
  rns <- rnorm(n, sd=sd)
  retained <- TRUE
  for(i in 1:n){
    y <- theta[i] + rns[i]
    a <- min(c(1,dnorm(y)/dnorm(theta[i])))
    retained[i+1] <- sample(c(TRUE,FALSE),1, prob=c(a, 1-a))
    if(retained[i+1]==TRUE){
      theta[i+1] <- y
    }
    else{
      theta[i+1] <- theta[i]
    }
  }
  list(fullchain=theta, sample=theta[retained])
}
set.seed(642134)
norm8 <- mh_mcmc_norm(10000, theta=8)
ts.plot(norm8$fullchain)

hist(norm8$sample)

ts.plot(norm8$fullchain[1:1000])

hist(norm8$sample[-c(1:178)])

set.seed(6421514)
norm8big <- mh_mcmc_norm(10000, theta=8, sd=52)
ts.plot(norm8big$fullchain)

ts.plot(norm8big$fullchain[1:1000])

hist(norm8big$sample[-c(1:5)])

set.seed(413514)

hist(norm8small$sample)

Bivariate Sampling

We then extended into the bivariate case to show that the MH algorithm easily extends to multivariate distributions.

library(mvtnorm)
mh_mcmc_bivnorm <- function(n, theta=c(8,8), trusig=matrix(c(1,.5,.5,1), 2), sd=0.2){
  rns <- matrix(rnorm(2*n, sd=sd), ncol=2)
  retained <- rep(TRUE, n+1)
  theta <- matrix(rep(theta, n+1), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
  for(i in 1:n){
    y <- theta[i,] + rns[i,]
    a <- min(c(1,dmvnorm(y, sigma=trusig)/dmvnorm(theta[i,], sigma=trusig)))
    retained[i+1] <- sample(c(TRUE,FALSE),1, prob=c(a, 1-a))
    if(retained[i+1]==TRUE){
      theta[i+1,] <- y
    }
    else{
      theta[i+1,] <- theta[i,]
    }
  }
  list(fullchain=theta, sample=theta[retained,])
}
set.seed(135432)
bivnorm8mod <- mh_mcmc_bivnorm(5000, sd=1)
ts.plot(bivnorm8mod$fullchain[,1], main="X1")

ts.plot(bivnorm8mod$fullchain[,2], main="X2")

zn = 100
seqx = seq(-5, 5, length.out = zn)
zval <- matrix(0, nrow=zn, ncol=zn)
for (i in 1:zn) zval[, i] = dmvnorm(cbind(seqx[i], seqx), sigma=matrix(c(1,.5,.5,1), 2))

contour(seqx, seqx, zval, levels = c(1e-04, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1), main = "Contour Plot")
lines(bivnorm8mod$fullchain)

contour(seqx, seqx, zval, levels = c(1e-04, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1), main = "Contour Plot")
lines(bivnorm8mod$fullchain[-c(1:500),])

contour(seqx, seqx, zval, levels = c(1e-04, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1), main = "Contour Plot")
points(bivnorm8mod$sample[-c(1:404),])

set.seed(135432)
bivnorm8 <- mh_mcmc_bivnorm(5000)

ts.plot(bivnorm8$fullchain[,1], main="X1")

ts.plot(bivnorm8$fullchain[,2], main="X2")
